sourcedFrom: SilencerCo Osprey 2.0 Field Manual — © 2022 SilencerCo, LLC (copyright line on the last page) (2022)
cleanIntro: ⛔ The Osprey 2.0 splits into two maintenance jobs that are nothing alike. The PISTON ASSEMBLY and the INDEXING SYSTEM are serviced regularly and come fully apart. The SILENCER ITSELF does not — SilencerCo says it will outlast the guns you put it on without the baffles ever being cleaned. Do the first two; leave the third.

steps.title: Firearm unloaded and the action OPEN before the can moves
steps.action: Open the action and see that the firearm is visibly clear of ammunition — before the silencer goes on and before it comes off. A suppressed gun is quieter, not safer, and the book says so in as many words.
steps.quote: Before installing the silencer on the host firearm, be sure the firearm is unloaded and the action is opened so the firearm is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey 2.0 Field Manual — © 2022 SilencerCo, LLC (copyright line on the last page) — WARNING

steps.title: ⛔ NO GAP at the shoulder — check the fit before firing
steps.action: This is the check that prevents a baffle strike. The thread mount must be FULLY shouldered against the barrel with no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the mount. If there is a gap, the silencer does not go on the gun that day.
steps.aside: Silencers must be free of obstructions such as mud, dirt, etc. DO NOT attempt to shoot through an obstructed silencer.
steps.quote: The thread mount must be fully shouldered on the barrel. There should be no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the silencer thread mount.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey 2.0 Field Manual — © 2022 SilencerCo, LLC (copyright line on the last page) — WARNING

steps.title: ⛔ Re-check tightness every 30 rounds
steps.action: Silencers back off under recoil, and a partly-unthreaded can is how baffle strikes happen. SilencerCo names an interval rather than leaving it to feel: verify the attachment is secure after about 30 discharges.
steps.quote: To ensure your silencer remains secure while firing, it is of the utmost importance that you frequently verify the silencer is securely tightened onto the barrel. We recommend checking the security of the attachment after 30 discharges of the firearm.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey 2.0 Field Manual — © 2022 SilencerCo, LLC (copyright line on the last page) — WARNING

steps.title: ⛔ Do NOT press the indexing button to unthread
steps.action: The button sets the can's orientation on the host; it is not a release. Pressing it while unthreading strips the threads. Take the Osprey off by turning it, button untouched, and it will return to the same orientation next time.
steps.quote: When unthreading, DO NOT push the button as this will cause threads to strip.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey 2.0 Field Manual — © 2022 SilencerCo, LLC (copyright line on the last page) — Mounting

steps.title: Piston assembly out — and a trick if it is stuck
steps.action: Remove the piston assembly with the provided Alpha Pistol tool and take all its parts apart. If it will not come out, thread the Osprey back onto the host, hold the indexing button DOWN and rotate the can back and forth for a few seconds — that breaks the carbon up — then release the button, take the can off and carry on.
steps.aside: If the assembly is difficult to remove, thread the Osprey 2.0 back onto the host weapon, hold the indexing button
steps.quote: The piston assembly should be cleaned regularly. Remove the assembly and disassemble all parts.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey 2.0 Field Manual — © 2022 SilencerCo, LLC (copyright line on the last page) — Servicing the Piston Assembly

steps.title: Scrub the piston parts, then grease ONE O-ring
steps.action: Scrubbing brush and cleaner over everything, all the carbon and buildup off. Then white lithium grease on the O-ring INSIDE the spring retainer, and the assembly goes back into the rear of the silencer. ⛔ No sandpaper, no blast media — the tolerances here are what make the piston work.
steps.aside: Never use hard abrasives such as sand paper or aluminum oxide blast media to clean your silencer components as this can ruin the finish and precise tolerances of your silencer, resulting in malfunction and further damage.
steps.quote: When finished, apply white lithium grease to the O-Ring inside the spring retainer, reinsert the piston assembly into the back of the silencer.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey 2.0 Field Manual — © 2022 SilencerCo, LLC (copyright line on the last page) — Servicing the Piston Assembly

steps.title: ⛔ Indexing system: photograph it before you touch it
steps.action: The indexing system is two pawls, two pins, two springs, a button, two screws and a back plate — and SilencerCo tells you to observe its position BEFORE disassembly because it must look exactly the same afterwards. The pawls must lie completely flat. Take the piston out first, then the two M3 torx screws and the back plate.
steps.aside: The indexing assembly should be regularly disassembled and cleaned.
steps.quote: Observe the position of the indexing system as it looks right now. You will want to ensure this system looks exactly the same once reassembled.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey 2.0 Field Manual — © 2022 SilencerCo, LLC (copyright line on the last page) — Indexing System

steps.title: ⛔ Clean the indexing parts DRY — no lubricant at all
steps.action: Scrubbing brush and cleaner on the indexing parts, and then nothing else: do NOT lubricate the indexing system, and make sure every part is dry before it goes back. A magnet helps with the pins; the two springs are loose and will fall if you let them.
steps.aside: Be careful not to lose the two springs, as they are loose and may fall.
steps.quote: DO NOT lubricate the indexing system. Ensure all parts are dry before assembling.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey 2.0 Field Manual — © 2022 SilencerCo, LLC (copyright line on the last page) — Indexing System

steps.title: ⛔ The silencer itself needs nothing — leave the baffles
steps.action: This is the part people get wrong. Aside from the piston assembly and the mounting surfaces, the Osprey 2.0 does not require regular maintenance: SilencerCo says it has enough internal volume to outlast the firearms you will mount it on without the baffles ever being cleaned. ⛔ And never submerge it or put it in an ultrasonic tank.
steps.aside: Do not completely submerge in chemical cleaner or use an ultrasonic cleaner, as this has the potential to damage the silencer.
steps.quote: Aside from the piston assembly and mounting surfaces, the Osprey 2.0 does not require regular maintenance.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Osprey 2.0 Field Manual — © 2022 SilencerCo, LLC (copyright line on the last page) — Maintenance

deepAbsentReason: SilencerCo publishes ONE level of disassembly for this silencer and it is the routine cleaning itself — the strip in the Assembly & Disassembly section is what an owner does every cleaning interval, not an occasional deep service. There is nothing deeper published, and nothing was borrowed: the SEALED SilencerCo cans in this same batch publish LESS, not more, so there is no sibling to take a deeper procedure from even if one were wanted.

cleaning.name: PISTON ASSEMBLY (regularly)
tasks: Out with the Alpha Pistol tool, fully disassembled
Scrubbing brush and cleaner, all carbon off
White lithium grease on the O-ring INSIDE the spring retainer

cleaning.name: INDEXING SYSTEM (regularly)
tasks: ⛔ Observe its position before anything moves
Two M3 torx screws, back plate, button, pawls, pins, springs
⛔ Cleaned DRY — no lubricant, all parts dry before reassembly

cleaning.name: MOUNTING SURFACES
tasks: Threads and shouldering surface clean; no gap at the shoulder

cleaning.name: ⛔ THE SILENCER BODY
tasks: Needs no regular maintenance — leave the baffles alone
⛔ Never submerged in cleaner, never ultrasonic
⛔ No hard abrasives on any component

reassembly: Indexing pawls, pins, springs and button back exactly as they came out — pawls lying completely flat.
Back plate on, two M3 torx screws in; ⛔ nothing in the indexing system lubricated and everything dry.
Piston assembly reassembled with white lithium grease on the spring-retainer O-ring, then back into the rear of the silencer.
Threaded onto the host until firmly secured, no barrel thread visible.
⛔ Orientation set with the indexing button — and NOT pressed when unthreading.
fncheck: ⛔ Check the O-ring inside the indexing ring / spring retainer before you trust it: the Osprey 2.0 will function without it, but it is what seals the gas when the piston actuates, and it is a wear item. With the can mounted, the indexing button sets orientation — set it, then remember not to press it when unthreading. Confirm no barrel thread is visible and there is no gap at the shoulder.
